title: [19.0.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`
message: `field` events are now queued onto the current `tail` file whenever any file is in flight. If payload order is `file A -> file B -> field for A`, that field will be attached to B instead of A, so the decoded FormData can still come out of order or lose the original grouping when multiple files are buffered concurrently. Consider tracking the file that was current when the field arrived, rather than always using the latest tail.

google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview.reason: The AI misunderstands how multipart streams work; events are emitted sequentially, so queueing fields on the `tail` (the most recently encountered file) correctly ensures they resolve in the exact same order they appeared in the payload.

Please verify the error handler always resolves or rejects the pending reply.

title: [19.2.x][FlightReply] Don't drop FormData entries in `decodeReplyFromBusboy`
message: Queued text fields are only flushed when the head file completes. If busboy ever emits a `field` after a later file has already completed but before the earlier head file ends, that field is attached to the tail file and delayed until the head finishes. That preserves payload order, but it also means a failure in the head file can now drop unrelated later fields that were already fully parsed. Please verify this is intended; otherwise fields may be lost on partial file failures.
